case_name: Elijah Servance and Corliss Servance v. Commissioner

taxpayer.notes: Mr. Servance worked 33 years for Metro-North Railroad, retired 2012 after colon cancer diagnosis. Notice of deficiency dated January 2, 2018. Pro se.

adjustments: $24,334 taxable tier 1 railroad retirement benefits (85% of $28,628)
$4,406 additional taxable wages from Hartford (Form W-2)
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Inclusion of tier 1 RRB benefits (claimed excludable under §104(a)(1)) and Hartford disability payments
conceded: Petitioners conceded liability for tax on the $61 dividends

findings_of_fact.fact: RRB paid Mr. Servance $28,628 tier 1 railroad retirement benefits in 2015 (stipulated), reported on SSA-1099; not reported on return
findings_of_fact.snippet: During 2015 the RRB paid Mr. Servance $28,628 in tier 1 railroad retirement benefits

findings_of_fact.fact: RRB disability application based on cancer granted December 19, 2012
findings_of_fact.snippet: His application was granted on December 19, 2012.

findings_of_fact.fact: No evidence cancer was caused by work for Metro-North
findings_of_fact.snippet: the record contains no evidence that Mr. Servance’s cancer was caused by his work for Metro-North

findings_of_fact.fact: No evidence of receipt of Hartford payments produced by respondent; Mr. Servance repaid Hartford Life Debt at $1,000/month beginning February 3, 2015
findings_of_fact.snippet: repaying the “Hartford Life Debt” at $1,000 per month beginning on February 3, 2015.

issues.question: Must petitioners include tier 1 railroad retirement benefits of $28,628 (to the extent of §86) in 2015 gross income, or are they excludable under §104(a)(1) as workmen's compensation?
issues.holding: Includible to the extent provided by §86 (85%); 45 U.S.C. §231a is not in the nature of a workmen's compensation act and no evidence of occupational illness
issues.computable_reason: Legal classification: tier 1 RRB are SS benefits under §86(d)(1)(B); §104(a)(1) inapplicable because statute not limited to on-the-job injury; 85% computation is §86 formula (inputs for base amount not stated)

issues.question: Must petitioners include $4,406 of Hartford long-term disability payments in 2015 gross income?
issues.holding: No; respondent failed threshold evidentiary burden for unreported income and petitioners credibly showed repayment (rescission doctrine)
issues.computable_reason: Turns on burden of proof, evidence, and credibility of repayment testimony

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: Tier 1 RRB included (85%); Hartford $4,406 not included; dividends conceded by petitioners; penalty conceded by respondent

notes: Some facts stipulated; receipt of $28,628 stipulated. Court did not verify §86 base-amount computation; it sustained inclusion "to the extent provided by section 86 (i.e., 85% of that amount)".
